newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Sept trade surplus falls to C$3.23 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada Sept trade surplus falls to C$3.23 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus fell in September to C$3.23 billion from C$3.73 billion in August (revised from C$4.02 billion), Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$3.99 billion in September. The survey also forecast imports of C$19.5 billion and exports of C$23.4 billion in the month.

Statistics Canada said exports rose for the third consecutive month fueled by rising sales of energy products and machinery. The gains in September helped increase total third quarter exports by 4.8 percent over the second quarter.
Exports to the United States, Canada's largest trading partner, accounted for the bulk of the September gains, the agency said.

Imports rose 4.6 percent in September from August, reaching a record level on the back of strong purchases of machinery and industrial goods. Shipments from all trading partners except the European Union increased.
